signals.description: Commanded operating point in plant units. On this rig the PLC command register sets motor VOLTAGE, not speed, and saturates at the supply rail, so this signal is produced by the calibrated piecewise lookup in raw_source_mapping.yaml:command_calibration — NOT by a linear scale. The previous linear scale (0.161172 rpm/count) capped it at 621 RPM for a motor that reaches 1082 RPM. Samples repaired by the register despike carry quality 2.
Actual motor/conveyor speed from encoder feedback

Motor TERMINAL voltage — the realised actuation, not an independent supply rail. It tracks the command register and clamps at 24.8 V; corr(voltage_v, speed_rpm) = 0.994 because the rig is open loop (speed = 39.27 RPM/V). Retained despite that collinearity because the residual around the ratio is the fault signal, and because it is the MPC's manipulated variable.
Supply current. Kept in RAW form for fast fault transients. At the native rate it is largely measurement noise (acf(1) = 0.205) — the load-carrying component is exposed separately as current_lp15_a.

setpoint_rpm - speed_rpm. SEMANTICS CHANGED 2026-08-04: this rig has no closed speed loop, so this is the deviation from the commanded level's own measured steady-state operating point, not a servo error. It remains the strongest single fault feature (std 21.3 RPM, acf(1) 0.407, |r| <= 0.07 against speed / voltage / setpoint).
Angular acceleration = speed_delta_rpm / dt, with dt measured from consecutive sample timestamps. Rate-normalised so the feature stays valid if the logger period changes.
Electrical input power = voltage_v * current_a. Included because a product is not reachable by the model's linear input layer.

15 s TRAILING mean of current_a. Raw current on this rig is acf(1) = 0.205 — noise with the load component buried in it; the trailing mean recovers it (acf(1) = 0.986 at n=15). 15 s is the knee between clearing the noise and smearing the ~5 s transient a jam produces. Also the MPC's second plant state, because raw current is not identifiable.

15 s TRAILING standard deviation of current_a (acf(1) = 0.978). Separates "noisy current" from "high current" — a distinction the raw channel cannot express, and the signature of commutation or mechanical roughness.

speed_rpm / voltage_v, guarded at voltage_v > 1 (reported as 0 when the motor is de-energised, which is a real operating state on this rig — 4 commanded stops). Median 39.27 RPM/V, CV 4.6%, and |r| <= 0.17 against EVERY other feature: the most genuinely independent signal in the set. A fall in RPM-per-volt at an unchanged command is what mechanical binding, belt overload or brush wear looks like, and neither speed nor voltage shows it alone.

Headroom to the configured limit = max_safe_current_a - current_a. Audit / telemetry signal only; excluded from the feature set because it is a constant minus a channel already present. The hard current block lives in safety_envelope.py.
PID controller output percentage. NOT present on this rig — the bench hardware is open loop (see DECISION_LOG.md [2026-08-04]).
